clue.text: Awkward cases caught in a doorway?

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the jumbled letters of cases
awkward suggests something ungainly and out of shape, so the letters of cases are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Clumsy packing cases get stuck in a doorway as someone tries to carry them through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' turns CASES into ACESS, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An access is a way in or entrance, which a doorway provides; the question mark flags the loose example.

clue.text: Hi-fi in Latin, I hear

definitions.meaning: concerning sound reproduction, as with stereo equipment
the Latin verb for to hear, in its first person singular form

explanation.definitionFit: Audio equipment is sound gear like a stereo, and the Latin word means literally I listen.

clue.text: It's out of the frying pan and into the soup!

definitions.text: It's out of the frying pan and into the soup!

parts.words: It's out of the frying pan and into the soup!
parts.note: plays on the proverb about going from bad to worse, but literally describes a cube of fried bread dropped into soup

explanation.surface: A twist on the old saying about escaping one trouble only to land in another.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of fried bread is cooked in a pan and then served floating in soup.

clue.text: Out in spring? Yes

parts.note: out in spring suggests being outdoors in springtime, but it describes plants pushing out new shoots in that season

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you will be outdoors in springtime and gets a brisk yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting or budding is what plants do in spring when they come out in new growth.

clue.text: Paper contains an unfounded rumour

indicators.note: contains tells us the word for paper holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: card is stiff paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper carries a baseless story.
explanation.definitionFit: A false report or hoax circulated as news, from the French word for duck.

clue.text: A lot to collect

parts.note: a mass is a large amount, a lot

explanation.surface: Someone has a great deal to gather together.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together or accumulate a large quantity of something.

clue.text: Lamb, say, is uncommonly unfathomable

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters of lamb and say appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A remark that lamb, for example, is extraordinarily deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal literally means as deep as an abyss, bottomless and too deep to measure.

clue.text: Yet such things don't cost the earth

definitions.text: Yet such things don't cost the earth

parts.words: Yet such things don't cost the earth
parts.note: the idiom about not costing the earth means cheap, while the things are cheap as soil, which is another word for earth

explanation.surface: A paradoxical remark about bargains that are inexpensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very cheap indeed, sold for next to nothing, as worthless as soil.

clue.text: Pickle jar, undo and put on the shelf

indicators.note: a pickle is a mess or muddle, so the letters of jar and undo are muddled

explanation.surface: Instructions to open a jar of pickle and put it on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like the jar's contents but signals rearranging JARUNDO.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve something is to postpone it, suspending a meeting until later.

clue.text: Neckline that may bring out a whistle

definitions.text: Neckline that may bring out a whistle

parts.words: Neckline that may bring out a whistle
parts.note: suggests a revealing dress that draws a wolf whistle, but means a cord round the neck that carries a whistle

explanation.surface: A plunging neckline that makes onlookers whistle in admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord worn around the neck, used by sailors or referees to hold a whistle or knife.

clue.text: Turn over in bed?

parts.note: turning over in bed is rolling about while lying down, but turning something over means considering it, done overnight

explanation.surface: A restless sleeper rolls over in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means delay a decision until the next day, thinking it over during the night.

clue.text: Restriction on entry may be lifted

definitions.text: Restriction on entry may be lifted

parts.words: Restriction on entry may be lifted
parts.note: lifting a restriction normally means relaxing a rule, but here a castle gate is physically raised

explanation.surface: Officials announce that limits on entry might be relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy grating at a castle gateway, raised to let people in and lowered to bar them.

clue.text: Staff employed in cooking

definitions.meaning: a ceremonial staff of office, carried before officials
a spice made from the outer covering of nutmeg

explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial rod of authority and also a spice from the husk of nutmeg.

clue.text: Bottled spirits

parts.note: bottled spirits suggests whisky or gin, but means magical beings trapped in lamps or bottles

explanation.surface: A shelf of spirits in bottles at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits of Arabian legend, like the one in Aladdin's lamp, are often said to be confined in a bottle.

clue.text: Soldiers armed with guns on manoeuvres

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters of armed and guns move into a new order

explanation.surface: Troops carrying weapons during an exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a guards regiment are soldiers, such as those at royal palaces.

clue.text: Mummy would fall apart were it not for him

definitions.text: Mummy would fall apart were it not for him

parts.words: Mummy would fall apart were it not for him
parts.note: sounds like a household that depends on a helpful man, but refers to a preserved Egyptian body

explanation.surface: A family where mother would collapse without the man of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who preserves corpses, as the ancient Egyptians did when making a mummy.

clue.text: Finance company issuing notes, not silver

parts.note: brass is informal British slang for money
a band is a group or company of people

explanation.surface: A finance firm that issues banknotes rather than coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A silver band is one made up of silver-plated instruments, so 'not silver' narrows the musical group to the other kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical group playing trumpets and cornets produces notes, distinct from a silver-plated band.

clue.text: Compelling someone to act, using whatever is available

definitions.meaning: forcing a person to carry something out

explanation.definitionFit: Forcing someone to perform an action, and also the idiom for managing with what you have.

clue.text: It's not right for in-law to embrace divorcee

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug, so the first pieces wrap around the next one

parts.note: split into in plus law, and an act is a law passed by parliament
an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: A remark that it is wrong for a relative by marriage to hug a former spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen disguises a split: 'in-law' looks like a relative by marriage, but its second half stands for a statute passed by parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaccurate or imprecise means falling short of being correct.

clue.text: A fabulous writer takes a retrospective pose

indicators.note: retrospective means looking backwards, so the word pose is read from end to start

explanation.surface: A great author strikes a nostalgic posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns POSE into ESOP. 'Fabulous' means writing fables, not merely wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek writer of fables, such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Like hell cats in a melee

indicators.note: a melee is a confused scrum, so the letters of cats in a are thrown together

explanation.surface: Fighting cats make a hellish noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the devil or the underworld, devilish and infernal.

clue.text: Woodcutter found wandering in a daze

indicators.note: wandering means straying about, so the letters of daze stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A lumberjack is found roaming about, dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe-like tool with an arched blade, used for shaping timber.

clue.text: Plant in peat, so it develops

indicators.note: develops means grows or changes form, so the letters of the fodder change their order

explanation.surface: A plant set in peat grows well.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican shrub with red bracts, popular as a Christmas houseplant.

clue.text: Flags outside the home

parts.note: suggests banners flown from a house, but flags are also flagstones laid as paving

explanation.surface: Banners hung outside a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved area beside a house, often laid with flagstones.

clue.text: I'd acted as a guide, yet didn't do much work

parts.note: taken as written, minus the apostrophe
to lead is to guide, so led is its past tense

explanation.surface: Someone who showed visitors around yet did little real work.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to laze or loaf about, doing nothing much.

clue.text: Reveals I have a thousand shares

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
parts are portions or shares

explanation.surface: Someone discloses owning a thousand shares in a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to disclose or pass on information.

clue.text: Isn't into cunning, being virtuous

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sly means cunning
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A good person is not given to craftiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly behaviour is very good and holy, morally upright.

clue.text: Thought it would be back in time

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the time word

parts.note: noon is a time of day

indicators.note: back means the word it is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a thing will return in time.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea or belief, something thought of.

clue.text: Possibly deduce it's extracted

indicators.note: possibly signals an alternative version of the word deduce, its letters in another order

explanation.surface: Someone may have reasoned out that it was drawn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or bring forth, as a conclusion from evidence.
